evidence: Parsed the shipped seed (environment/assets/seed_data.json, 28549 bytes, UTF-8, no BOM, ASCII only; solution copy byte-identical, sha256 a1c65c806b54...3740 matches manifest.json lines 9/24) with an in-memory Python script. Referential integrity: 10 users, 3 jobs, 16 applications, 127 messages, 3 notes, 6 read markers; all ids unique; every job.recruiter_id resolves to a recruiter and every manager_id to a hiring_manager; every application.job_id, message.application_id/sender_id, note.application_id/author_id and read.user_id/application_id resolves - no orphans. Board consistency: every stage is one of the six listed; positions per (job,stage) are contiguous 1..n; Interview counts 2/3 (JOB-PLAT), 1/2 (JOB-DATA), 1/3 (JOB-DSGN) are within interview_limit; only APP-301 is REJECTED and it carries rejected_from=SCREEN plus a non-blank reason, no other card has stray reject fields; no duplicate email within a job (Noor Haddad on APP-101 JOB-PLAT and APP-302 JOB-DSGN is allowed by hireops_rules.md:33); candidate_status_labels keys equal stages and match the table at hireops_rules.md:183-190; thread_page_size 30 matches hireops_rules.md:144. Permission consistency: every message sender may write in that conversation under hireops_rules.md:131-134 (recruiters, or the candidate whose email owns the application); every note author is a recruiter or the job's own manager (MGR1 on JOB-PLAT, MGR3 on JOB-DSGN) per :104-105; candidate user names match their applications' candidate_name. Timestamps are strictly increasing within each conversation; APP-101 has 120 messages, matching app_context.md:29-30. Every read_count <= the conversation length. Facts the judges quote are consistent with the seed: functional Z expects Lena's unread=1 on Product Designer (APP-301: CAN3 read_count 2 of 3, msg 3 by REC3 -> 1), Applied order Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi and Screen order Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz (positions 1..3/1..2), and note text 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' (exact seed note). Clean: all people synthetic; all emails on RFC 2606 reserved domains hireops.example, candidates.example, mail.example; no phone numbers, addresses, DOBs, URLs or http links; regex scan for <, >, javascript:, onerror, ${, {{, 'ignore', 'system prompt', password/token/secret/api key, SQL keywords and grade/score/judge/rubric/criteri returned nothing. No credential in the seed itself (the shared demo password lives only in instruction.md:17 and hireops_rules.md:11, which the skill profile and the workbook's internal annotation treat as expected). generated_note is a benign pointer to /instructions/hireops_rules.md. Non-blocking observations (no grading impact found): (a) three read markers trail the reader's own latest message - USR-CAN1 on APP-101 read_count 119 though CAN1 sent #120; USR-REC3 on APP-301 read_count 2 though REC3 sent #3; USR-REC3 has no marker on APP-302 though REC3 sent its only message. hireops_rules.md:152-153 says own messages are never unread and sending counts as read, so every conforming reading yields the same unread counts (own messages excluded) and the same seen marks (REC1 marker 120 covers CAN1 #120; CAN3 marker 2 vs REC3 #3 -> not seen; no candidate message is affected), so I could not construct a conforming app graded differently. golden db.js:82-83 maps read_count to last_read_id and treats missing markers as none. (b) Narrative only: APP-301 is rejected from Screen while REC3's 07-29 message says 'We will write again once the panel has met'; rejection time is not seeded, so this is not a data contradiction. Counterexample attempts: a broken app that ignores read markers would show Lena unread=3 and fail Z, so the seed discriminates; a conforming app that clamps markers to the user's last own message gives identical observable values, so it is not penalised. Deterministic check-fixtures parse and check-probe-not-in-seed are covered by the separate deterministic reviewer; I did not run the private checkers. No runtime execution was needed for this static-data row.
